title.en: Kubernetes: EKS, Auto Mode, Pod Identity, and ALB

sources.title: Amazon EKS architecture
supports: Every cluster has its own Kubernetes control plane, not shared with other clusters or accounts
The control plane has at least two API server instances and three etcd instances across three Availability Zones
EKS replaces a control plane instance that fails

sources.title: Automate cluster infrastructure with EKS Auto Mode
supports: Auto Mode manages compute autoscaling, pod and service networking, application load balancing, cluster DNS, and block storage as core components instead of add-ons
Nodes are EC2 managed instances running Bottlerocket variants; SSH and SSM access to them is not allowed
Nodes have a maximum lifetime of 21 days, which can be reduced
Upgrades respect Pod Disruption Budgets; intervention might be required if a blocking budget prevents an update
The EKS Pod Identity Agent does not have to be installed on Auto Mode clusters
Auto scaling relies on Karpenter
Since April 22, 2026 new managed instances are hidden by default from EC2 console views and list APIs

sources.title: Create a Node Pool for EKS Auto Mode
supports: The built-in system and general-purpose node pools cannot be modified, only enabled or disabled
A cluster can be created with nodePools and nodeRoleArn both empty; then no default NodeClass exists, and a custom NodeClass, an access entry for its role, and a custom NodePool are needed
A NodePool is a karpenter.sh/v1 object whose nodeClassRef names group eks.amazonaws.com, kind NodeClass
Supported requirement labels include kubernetes.io/arch, karpenter.sh/capacity-type, and node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
By default Auto Mode consolidates underutilized instances, terminates instances after 336 hours, and sets one disruption budget of 10% of nodes
limits.cpu and limits.memory bound what a node pool may provision

sources.title: Enable or Disable Built-in NodePools
supports: general-purpose uses only the amd64 architecture; system supports amd64 and arm64 and carries a CriticalAddonsOnly taint
Both built-in pools use on-demand capacity, the C, M, and R families, and generation 5 or newer
At least one built-in pool must be enabled for EKS to provision the default NodeClass

sources.title: Create a Node Class for Amazon EKS
supports: A NodeClass is an eks.amazonaws.com/v1 object with role, subnetSelectorTerms, securityGroupSelectorTerms, ephemeralStorage, and advancedNetworking
advancedNetworking.associatePublicIPAddress controls whether instances get a public IP address; unset, it follows the subnet's MapPublicIpOnLaunch
A custom node class needs an access entry of type EC2 with the AmazonEKSAutoNodePolicy access policy, or its nodes cannot join; the page gives the CloudFormation for it
subnetSelectorTerms and securityGroupSelectorTerms select by tags or by id; nodes are distributed across the matching subnets
ephemeralStorage.size accepts 1 to 59000Gi; the specification example shows 80Gi, iops 3000 and throughput 125

sources.title: Create an IngressClass to configure an Application Load Balancer
supports: An IngressClass with controller eks.amazonaws.com/alb and an IngressClassParams (eks.amazonaws.com/v1) make Auto Mode create an ALB for an Ingress
IngressClassParams fields include scheme, subnets.ids, and subnets.matchTags (filters with a key and a list of values); targetType defaults to ip
IngressClass annotations cannot configure the load balancer; annotations on individual Ingress resources can
The page lists the Ingress annotations that are not supported; the health check and target group attribute annotations are not on that list
Deleting the Ingress makes Auto Mode delete the load balancer
The page does not mention the Gateway API
sources.note: Whether each health check annotation of the open source controller takes effect under Auto Mode was not confirmed beyond its absence from the unsupported list.

sources.title: Learn about VPC Networking and Load Balancing in EKS Auto Mode
supports: Auto Mode supports nodes and pods in public or private subnets
Security groups per pod and alternate CNI plugins are not supported
CoreDNS runs as a system service on each node, not as a Deployment
The default target mode of load balancers is IP
The EKS managed policy only lets EKS modify security groups named eks-cluster-sg-*; nodes with other security groups need extra permissions on the cluster role

sources.title: Tag subnets for EKS Auto Mode
supports: Subnets used for load balancing by Auto Mode need the tag kubernetes.io/role/elb (public) or kubernetes.io/role/internal-elb (private)

sources.title: Learn about Amazon EKS Auto Mode Managed instances
supports: Auto Mode supports the t4g family among others
Auto Mode only creates instances with more than 1 CPU whose size is not nano, micro, or small
EKS generally releases a new AMI each week
IMDSv2 with a hop limit of 1 is enforced and cannot be changed

sources.title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode cluster IAM role
supports: The suggested managed policies are AmazonEKSClusterPolicy, AmazonEKSComputePolicy, AmazonEKSBlockStoragePolicyV2, AmazonEKSLoadBalancingPolicy, and AmazonEKSNetworkingPolicy
The trust policy allows sts:AssumeRole and sts:TagSession for eks.amazonaws.com

sources.title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode node IAM role
supports: The node role trusts ec2.amazonaws.com and carries AmazonEKSWorkerNodeMinimalPolicy and AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryPullOnly

sources.title: Create an EKS Auto Mode Cluster with the AWS CLI
supports: The create-cluster request enables computeConfig, kubernetesNetworkConfig.elasticLoadBalancing, and storageConfig.blockStorage, and sets accessConfig.authenticationMode to API
The example enables both the public and the private endpoint
sources.note: The page's request does not set bootstrapSelfManagedAddons. aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0 refuses true with Auto Mode (see aws-cdk-lib-eks); what happens when it is omitted was not confirmed.

sources.title: Enable EKS Auto Mode on an existing cluster
supports: The compute, block storage, and load balancing capabilities must all be enabled or disabled in the same request

sources.title: Update the Kubernetes Version of an EKS Auto Mode cluster
supports: After a control plane upgrade Auto Mode replaces nodes as they expire, with nodes of the new version, observing pod disruption budgets
The VPC CNI, the load balancer controller, CoreDNS, kube-proxy, Karpenter, and the EBS CSI driver no longer need updating by the user

sources.title: Manage compute resources by using nodes
supports: With managed node groups you must deploy and manage EC2 instances, patch the operating system, and update the node AMI and Kubernetes version yourself; with Auto Mode you do not
Auto Mode nodes cannot be reached by SSH, cannot run a custom AMI or CNI, and cannot run Windows containers
Auto Mode charges a separate fee on top of the EC2 instance price

sources.title: Simplify compute management with AWS Fargate
supports: Pods on Fargate run only in private subnets with NAT gateway access
DaemonSets, privileged containers, and GPUs are not supported on Fargate
The comparison table says Fargate cannot run workloads that require Arm processors

sources.title: Learn how EKS Pod Identity grants pods access to AWS services
supports: An association maps an IAM role to a service account in a namespace of a cluster
The role's trust policy names the service principal pods.eks.amazonaws.com; no OIDC provider is involved
EKS sets environment variables in the pod's containers so that the AWS SDKs use the Pod Identity credentials
Up to 5,000 associations per cluster
Associations are eventually consistent, with delays of several seconds
Pod Identity is not available for pods on Fargate or on Windows instances
Containers are not a security boundary; pods on the same node share a kernel

sources.title: Assign an IAM role to a Kubernetes service account
supports: The trust policy allows sts:AssumeRole and sts:TagSession
The namespace and the service account of an association may be named before they exist in the cluster

sources.title: Understand how EKS Pod Identity works
supports: The pod gets AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI pointing at http://169.254.170.23/v1/credentials and AWS_CONTAINER_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN_FILE

sources.title: Grant Kubernetes workloads access to AWS using Kubernetes Service Accounts
supports: AWS recommends EKS Pod Identity over IRSA whenever possible
IRSA needs an IAM OIDC provider per cluster (default limit of 100 per account) and the cluster's provider in each role's trust policy
With IRSA the SDK in the pod calls sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity itself
IRSA also works outside EKS (EKS Anywhere, OpenShift on AWS, self-managed clusters); Pod Identity is EKS only

sources.title: Grant IAM users access to Kubernetes with EKS access entries
supports: An access entry associates Kubernetes permissions with an IAM identity, through an access policy or a Kubernetes group
Access is managed through the EKS API, and can be restored there without access to the Kubernetes API

sources.title: Review access policy permissions
supports: AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy allows every verb on every resource
AmazonEKSEditPolicy allows create, delete, patch, and update on deployments, services, service accounts, ingresses, and pod disruption budgets, and only read access to namespaces
AmazonEKSAutoNodePolicy exists for Auto Mode nodes

sources.title: Understand the Kubernetes version lifecycle on EKS
supports: A minor version is in standard support for 14 months after its release on EKS, then in extended support for 12 months
Extended support is enabled by default; at its end the cluster is auto-upgraded to the oldest version still in extended support
On 2026-10-13 standard support covered 1.37, 1.36, 1.35, and 1.34; extended support covered 1.33, 1.32, and 1.31
The release calendar: 1.37 leaves standard support on December 1, 2027; 1.34 on December 2, 2026
A cluster upgraded in place can be rolled back to the previous minor version within 7 days
Billing for extended support starts at the beginning of the day (UTC) that standard support ends

sources.title: Prevent increased cluster costs by disabling EKS extended support
supports: With the upgrade policy STANDARD the cluster is automatically upgraded to the next version at the end of standard support
Extended support cannot be disabled once the cluster has entered it

sources.title: Update existing cluster to new Kubernetes version
supports: A cluster is updated one minor version at a time
An update needs up to five available IP addresses in the cluster's subnets
kubectl must be within one minor version of the control plane
After the 7-day window a cluster cannot be downgraded

sources.title: Delete a cluster
supports: Ingress resources should be deleted before the cluster; otherwise the Application Load Balancer remains after the cluster is deleted
For Auto Mode the page says that all nodes and all load balancers will be deleted with the cluster
Deletion protection must be disabled before a cluster can be deleted
sources.note: The two statements about load balancers stand side by side on the page. This chapter deletes the Ingress first.

sources.title: Route internet traffic with AWS Load Balancer Controller
supports: Outside Auto Mode the controller is installed into the cluster, with Helm for example
From version 2.14.0 the controller creates an ALB for a Kubernetes Gateway

sources.title: Simplify node lifecycle with managed node groups
supports: Every managed node is part of an EC2 Auto Scaling group that EKS manages, in your account
Managed node groups are tagged for discovery by the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler

sources.title: Set up the Amazon EKS Pod Identity Agent
supports: Outside Auto Mode the Pod Identity Agent is installed as an EKS add-on

sources.title: Assign IAM roles to Kubernetes service accounts
supports: With IRSA the service account is annotated with eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn

sources.title: Roll back a cluster to a previous Kubernetes version
supports: A rollback must be started within 7 days of the upgrade completing

sources.title: Connect kubectl to an EKS cluster by creating a kubeconfig file
supports: aws eks update-kubeconfig --region ... --name ... writes the kubeconfig entry; authentication uses aws eks get-token

sources.title: Set up kubectl and eksctl
supports: kubectl must be within one minor version of the cluster's control plane

sources.title: Troubleshoot EKS Auto Mode
supports: kubectl get nodeclaim and kubectl describe nodeclaim show why a node has not joined the cluster

sources.title: kubectl apply
supports: kubectl apply takes a configuration by file name or stdin; the examples include applying JSON passed into stdin

sources.title: kubectl diff
supports: kubectl diff shows the difference between the live configuration and the one that would be applied

sources.title: Amazon EKS pricing
supports: USD 0.10 per cluster per hour in standard support; USD 0.60 per cluster per hour in extended support, which includes the 0.10
Auto Mode charges are in addition to the EC2 instance price, per second with a one-minute minimum, and independent of the EC2 purchase option
Worker nodes' EC2 instances, EBS volumes, and public IPv4 addresses are billed on top

sources.title: Amazon ECS pricing
supports: There is no additional charge for Amazon ECS orchestration

sources.title: AWS Price List: AmazonEKS, ap-northeast-1
supports: APN1-AmazonEKS-Hours:perCluster is USD 0.10 per hour
APN1-AmazonEKS-Hours:extendedSupport is USD 0.50 per hour, charged on top of the cluster hour
APN1-EKS-Auto:t4g.medium-management-hours is USD 0.00518 per hour

sources.title: AWS Price List: AmazonEC2, ap-northeast-1 (t4g.medium)
supports: APN1-BoxUsage:t4g.medium, Linux, shared tenancy, is USD 0.0432 per hour; the type has 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB
sources.note: Publication date 2026-10-09T20:31:34Z. That Auto Mode's Bottlerocket nodes are billed at the Linux rate is this chapter's assumption.

sources.title: AWS::EKS::Cluster
supports: AccessConfig.AuthenticationMode defaults to CONFIG_MAP when a cluster is created through CloudFormation; allowed values are CONFIG_MAP, API_AND_CONFIG_MAP, and API
BootstrapClusterCreatorAdminPermissions defaults to true
UpgradePolicy.SupportType defaults to EXTENDED; STANDARD disables extended support
BootstrapSelfManagedAddons false means vpc-cni, coredns, and kube-proxy are not installed
DeletionProtection true prevents deletion until it is disabled
Without Version the default version is used, which might not be the latest
sources.note: Read together with the property pages for ComputeConfig, AccessConfig, and UpgradePolicy.

sources.title: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0: aws-eks and aws-eks-v2
supports: aws-eks/lib/eks.generated.d.ts declares CfnCluster with computeConfig, kubernetesNetworkConfig.elasticLoadBalancing, storageConfig.blockStorage, accessConfig, upgradePolicy, bootstrapSelfManagedAddons, and deletionProtection; CfnAccessEntry; and CfnPodIdentityAssociation
aws-eks-v2/lib/cluster.js throws when bootstrapSelfManagedAddons is true with Auto Mode
aws-eks-v2's Auto Mode roles attach AmazonEKSBlockStoragePolicy and AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, not the V2 and Minimal policies that today's user guide lists
sources.note: Read from the installed package. The synthesis experiment with eks-v2 is described in the chapter's verification notes.

sources.title: cdkd 0.296.28: how AWS::EKS types are routed
supports: No SDK provider is registered for any AWS::EKS type
AWS::EKS::Cluster, AccessEntry, and PodIdentityAssociation are not on the list of types Cloud Control cannot provision, so they are routed to Cloud Control API
Cloud Control operations on AWS::EKS::Cluster are given 30 minutes to create and 30 minutes to delete
cdkd knows DeletionProtection as the protection property of AWS::EKS::Cluster
AWS::IAM::Role has an SDK provider that handles AssumeRolePolicyDocument and ManagedPolicyArns
sources.note: Read from the bundled dist of the installed npm package (the bundle keeps the source file names: provisioning/provider-registry.ts, unsupported-types.generated.ts, slow-cc-operation-timeouts.ts, protection-flags.ts, property-coverage.generated.ts). Nothing was deployed.

sources.title: Kubernetes: Deployments
supports: maxUnavailable is calculated from a percentage by rounding down, maxSurge by rounding up; both default to 25%
maxUnavailable cannot be 0 if maxSurge is 0, and the reverse
progressDeadlineSeconds defaults to 600; Kubernetes takes no action on a stalled Deployment other than to report a status condition
minReadySeconds is how long a new pod must be ready before it counts as available

sources.title: Kubernetes: Specifying a Disruption Budget for your Application
supports: A budget has a selector and exactly one of minAvailable and maxUnavailable, each a number or a percentage
A minAvailable percentage rounds up; a maxUnavailable percentage rounds up the number of pods that may be disrupted
A budget does not guarantee the number of pods: a node may still fail

sources.title: Kubernetes: Disruptions
supports: Draining a node is a voluntary disruption and goes through the eviction API, which respects budgets; deleting pods or deployments directly bypasses them
Pods unavailable because of a rolling upgrade count against the budget, but a Deployment is not limited by budgets when it rolls
Involuntary disruptions cannot be prevented by a budget, but count against it
The AlwaysAllow unhealthy pod eviction policy is recommended so that a misbehaving application cannot block a drain

sources.title: Kubernetes: API-initiated Eviction
supports: An eviction the budget does not allow is answered with 429 Too Many Requests

sources.title: Kubernetes: Pod Lifecycle
supports: The grace period defaults to 30 seconds; a preStop hook runs first and its time counts against the grace period
The kubelet sends TERM to process 1 of each container, and KILL when the grace period has expired
At the same time as the kubelet starts the graceful shutdown, the control plane removes the pod from EndpointSlices

sources.title: Kubernetes: Container Lifecycle Hooks
supports: Hook handlers are Exec, HTTP, and Sleep; Sleep pauses the container for a given duration and is run by the kubelet

sources.title: Kubernetes: Pod Topology Spread Constraints
supports: maxSkew is how unevenly pods may be distributed; whenUnsatisfiable is DoNotSchedule by default

sources.title: AWS Load Balancer Controller: Ingress annotations
supports: alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/healthcheck-path, healthcheck-interval-seconds, healthcheck-timeout-seconds, healthy-threshold-count, unhealthy-threshold-count, success-codes, and target-group-attributes exist with these names and take string values
sources.note: This is the documentation of the open source controller, not of Auto Mode's built-in one.

sources.title: docker-node: Best Practices (non-root user)
supports: The node images provide the user node with uid 1000

sources.title: Cloudflare Containers
supports: Containers are started on demand and controlled by code in a Worker, through a Durable Object
The page contrasts this with writing Kubernetes operators; it offers no Kubernetes API
Available on the Workers Paid plan

sources.title: Cloudflare Containers: Lifecycle of a Container
supports: Images should be built for the linux/amd64 architecture

sources.title: Cloudflare Containers: FAQ
supports: Built-in autoscaling for stateless applications is not available today
On a host stop the container gets SIGTERM, up to 15 minutes, then SIGKILL

sources.title: Vercel: Container Runtime
supports: Container Runtime is in beta on all plans: Vercel Functions run an OCI image built from a Dockerfile.vercel
Functions scale up and down automatically and use Active CPU pricing
The page offers no Kubernetes API

sources.title: Vercel: Runtimes
supports: Container is listed among the runtimes of Vercel Functions

glossary.ja: コントロールプレーン

definition.ja: Kubernetes の API サーバーと、クラスターの状態を持つ etcd など、クラスターを管理する側の部品。EKS では AWS が動かし、クラスター 1 つごとに時間で課金される。
definition.en: The managing side of a Kubernetes cluster: the API server, etcd with the cluster's state, and the controllers. On EKS, AWS runs it and bills it by the hour, per cluster.

definition.ja: Kubernetes が動かす最小の単位。1 つ以上のコンテナと、それらが共有するネットワークからなる。ECS のタスクに当たる。
definition.en: The smallest thing Kubernetes runs: one or more containers and the network they share. What a task is on ECS.

definition.ja: Pod を載せるマシン。EKS では EC2 のインスタンスで、Pod はノードの CPU とメモリを分け合う。
definition.en: A machine that pods run on. On EKS it is an EC2 instance, and the pods on it share its CPU and memory.

definition.ja: ノードの起動と入れ替え、ロードバランサー、Pod のネットワーク、ブロックストレージを EKS が受け持つ動かし方。ノードは利用者のアカウントの EC2 インスタンスだが、ログインも AMI の指定もできない。
definition.en: A way to run EKS in which EKS itself starts and replaces nodes and runs load balancing, pod networking, and block storage. The nodes are EC2 instances in your account, but you cannot log in to them or choose their AMI.

definition.ja: Auto Mode（Karpenter）が起動してよいノードの条件と上限を書いた Kubernetes のオブジェクト。CPU アーキテクチャ、インスタンスタイプ、合計の vCPU などを決める。
definition.en: A Kubernetes object that says which nodes Auto Mode (Karpenter) may start and how many: architecture, instance types, total vCPUs.

definition.ja: クラスター、namespace、service account の組に IAM ロールを結び付ける仕組み。結び付けは EKS の API に持ち、ロールの信頼ポリシーは pods.eks.amazonaws.com を許すだけで済む。
definition.en: A way to tie an IAM role to a service account in a namespace of a cluster. The association lives in the EKS API, and the role's trust policy only has to name pods.eks.amazonaws.com.

definition.ja: IAM のロールやユーザーに、Kubernetes の API で何をしてよいかを結び付ける EKS の設定。クラスターの中の ConfigMap ではなく EKS の API で管理する。
definition.en: An EKS setting that ties an IAM role or user to what it may do through the Kubernetes API. It is managed through the EKS API, not in a ConfigMap inside the cluster.

definition.ja: ノードの drain のような意図した中断で、同時に欠けてよい Pod の数を決める Kubernetes のオブジェクト。ノードの故障は止められない。
definition.en: A Kubernetes object that limits how many pods a voluntary disruption, such as draining a node, may take away at once. It cannot stop a node from failing.

definition.ja: クラスターの外から来た HTTP を、どの Service へ送るかを書いた Kubernetes のオブジェクト。EKS では、これを見たコントローラーが Application Load Balancer を作る。
definition.en: A Kubernetes object that says which Service HTTP from outside the cluster goes to. On EKS a controller reads it and creates an Application Load Balancer.

definition.ja: Kubernetes のマイナーバージョンが EKS の標準サポート（公開から 14 か月）を過ぎたあとの 12 か月。クラスターの時間料金が上がる。
definition.en: The 12 months after a Kubernetes minor version leaves EKS standard support (14 months from release). The cluster's hourly price rises for that time.

note.ja: クラスターが無い。kubectl は devShell に入ったが、マニフェストは API サーバーに一度も渡していない
note.en: There is no cluster. kubectl is now in the devShell, but the manifests were never given to an API server

note.ja: flake.nix の devShell に `pkgs.kubectl` を足し、`nix develop` の中で実行した。Client Version は v1.37.1、Kustomize は v5.8.1。スタックのクラスターは 1.37 なので、1 マイナーバージョン以内に入っている。クラスターには接続していない
note.en: `pkgs.kubectl` was added to the devShell in flake.nix and the command was run inside `nix develop`. Client Version v1.37.1, Kustomize v5.8.1. The stack's cluster is 1.37, so the client is within one minor version. No cluster was contacted

summary.ja: 34章のスタックを一度もデプロイしていない。cdkd 0.296.28 は AWS::EKS の種類に専用の実装を持たず、Cloud Control API を経由する。クラスターの作成と削除、アクセスエントリー、Pod Identity の関連付け、別のアプリのスタックからの Fn::ImportValue が通るかは未確認。
summary.en: The chapter 34 stack has never been deployed. cdkd 0.296.28 has no provider of its own for AWS::EKS types and goes through Cloud Control API. Unverified: creating and deleting the cluster, the access entries, the Pod Identity association, and Fn::ImportValue from another app's stack.

resume.ja: `vp run net:infra:deploy`、`vp run eks:infra:diff`、`vp run eks:infra:deploy` の順に実行し、`aws eks describe-cluster --name aih-eks` で status が ACTIVE になること、computeConfig、accessConfig、upgradePolicy がテンプレートどおりであることを確かめる。終わったら `vp run eks:infra:destroy`。
resume.en: Run `vp run net:infra:deploy`, `vp run eks:infra:diff`, and `vp run eks:infra:deploy` in that order, then check with `aws eks describe-cluster --name aih-eks` that the status is ACTIVE and that computeConfig, accessConfig, and upgradePolicy are what the template says. Finish with `vp run eks:infra:destroy`.

summary.ja: k8s/ のマニフェストを API サーバーに渡したことがない。自前の NodeClass（パブリックサブネット、associatePublicIPAddress）でノードが起動してクラスターに参加するか、t4g.medium が選ばれるか、Name タグで ALB のサブネットを選べるか、Ingress の annotation が Auto Mode で効くか、preStop の 15 秒で足りるか、Pod Identity の認証情報が Pod に届くかは未確認。
summary.en: The manifests in k8s/ were never given to an API server. Unverified: that nodes of the custom NodeClass (public subnets, associatePublicIPAddress) start and join, that t4g.medium is what gets launched, that the load balancer's subnets can be chosen by the Name tag, that the Ingress annotations take effect under Auto Mode, that 15 seconds of preStop are enough, and that Pod Identity credentials reach the pod.

resume.ja: クラスターをデプロイし、kubectl を用意して `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name aih-eks --region ap-northeast-1`、`vp run eks:manifests cluster | kubectl apply -f -`、`vp run eks:manifests app --tag v1 | kubectl apply -f -` を実行する。`kubectl get nodes -o wide`、`kubectl -n notes get pods,ingress` を見て、Ingress のホスト名へ `curl -si .../health` を送る。`kubectl -n notes rollout restart deployment/notes-api` の間、12章の `vp run ecs:watch --url http://<host>` でエラーが出ないことを確かめる。
resume.en: Deploy the cluster, get kubectl, and run `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name aih-eks --region ap-northeast-1`, `vp run eks:manifests cluster | kubectl apply -f -`, and `vp run eks:manifests app --tag v1 | kubectl apply -f -`. Look at `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `kubectl -n notes get pods,ingress`, and send `curl -si .../health` to the Ingress host name. During `kubectl -n notes rollout restart deployment/notes-api`, watch with chapter 12's `vp run ecs:watch --url http://<host>` that no request fails.

summary.ja: devShell の kubectl（1.37.1）は flake.lock が固定する nixpkgs のもので、34章のクラスターのバージョン（1.37）とは別々に変わる。nixpkgs の固定かクラスターのバージョンのどちらかを更新すると、1 マイナーバージョン以内でなくなることがある。この kubectl をクラスターに対して使ったことはない。
summary.en: The devShell's kubectl (1.37.1) comes from the nixpkgs that flake.lock pins, and it changes independently of chapter 34's cluster version (1.37). Updating either the nixpkgs pin or the cluster version can take the two more than one minor version apart. This kubectl has never been used against a cluster.

resume.ja: flake.lock かクラスターのバージョンを更新したら、`nix develop -c sh -c 'kubectl version --client'` の結果とクラスターのバージョンを比べ、34章の deploy のページの版と `data/fragments/34.json` の toolchain を直す。
resume.en: After updating flake.lock or the cluster version, compare the output of `nix develop -c sh -c 'kubectl version --client'` with the cluster version, and update the version on chapter 34's deploy page and the toolchain entry in `data/fragments/34.json`.
